t: You're on the South Bank, where the Dome of Discovery once stood. It was a temporary exhibition building, put up for the Festival of Britain in 1951 beside the River Thames. The architect was Ralph Tubbs, who lived from 1912 to 1996, and this is the building he is best known for. The engineers were Freeman Fox and Partners, in particular Oleg Kerensky and Gilbert Roberts. The dome is gone now, but the festival it served was a great success, and this was one of its main attractions.
